Flaxman orcid: 0000-0001-6033-4713 corresponding: true email: abie@ihme.washington.edu affiliations: - department: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation name: University of Washington address: "Population Health Building/Hans Rosling Center, 3980 15th Ave. NE, UW Campus Box #351615" city: Seattle region: WA postal-code: "98195" country: USA - name: Anders Alexandersson # TODO before submission: confirm affiliation wording, add full street address and ORCID affiliations: - department: Florida Cancer Data System name: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine city: Miami region: FL country: USA abstract: | **Introduction** … **Methods** … **Results** … **Conclusion** … keywords: [record linkage, entity resolution, simulated data, cancer registry, benchmark dataset, reproducibility, pseudopeople] --- ::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"} ::: {#author-block .cell execution_count=1} **Author affiliations** | **Abraham D. Flaxman** (corresponding author), ORCID 0000-0001-6033-4713 | Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, University of Washington, Population Health Building/Hans Rosling Center, 3980 15th Ave. NE, UW Campus Box #351615, Seattle WA 98195, USA | Email: abie@ihme.washington.edu | **Anders Alexandersson** | Florida Cancer Data System, University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, Miami FL, USA ::: ::: ## Key Features {.unnumbered} - **What is unique:** a large, fully simulated, multi-file dataset for linking individual people, with cross-file ground truth (every record carries a `simulant_id`, so missed-match and false-match rates of any method can be computed exactly rather than estimated), designed to capture the record matching challenges faced by a Florida-scale cancer data system. - **Why created:** linkage software for cancer registries must be developed and tested on names, dates of birth, addresses and SSNs, which are exactly the identifiers that confidentiality rules prevent registries from releasing. - **Details:** a simulated population of Florida residents based on the 2020 population of 21\,123\,234 simulants, including a cancer registry of 5\,000\,006 records where the age and sex structure matches the age- and sex-specific cancer incidence pattern of the Florida Cancer Data System, as well as researcher finder files of 500\,001 and 100\,000 records. - **Data linkage:** the larger finder file includes 100\,000 simulants in the registry and the smaller finder file includes 20\,000 simulants. There is no overlap between the finder files. - **Main categories of data:** simulated person-level identifiers including name, date of birth, sex, street-address fields, SSN, race/ethnicity, carrying realistic synthetic noise (typos, nicknames, month/day swaps, blanks, duplications). - **Access:** direct download under a permissive licence with a DOI. # Background … # Methods ## Generating simulated records with pseudopeople ::: {.cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pseudopeople as psp census = psp.generate_decennial_census() # bundled ~10k-simulant sample census.head() ``` ::: {#sample-demo .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
